GDET50 failed (20/30, scale20 2/12) with the 600 s case guard firing on 29 scale20 records, and GQB25 failed (max chunk 90.5 s, 25 case walls over 600 s) (Exact). Observed in 050: slowest scale20 rate 4503 conflicts/s (11730023, 607.5 s, 8 workers shared with the other parts); scale20 records with no guard firing 9563 to 20323 conflicts/s; per-chunk rate as low as about 550 conflicts/s (90.5 s for 50000); slowest clean 12-state rate 30256 conflicts/s (1500135 conflicts in 49.6 s); the single decided scale20 case needed about 3.25M conflicts; control 11750001 spent B12 = 1500000 (IDU, no guard). Reading (Inferred): re-planning B20 alone, by plan 050's rule, gives B20 about 2.0M, below the 3.25M the one decided case needed, so a budget cut alone would likely make the 20-state gate vacuous; the runtime fix therefore has three parts: B20 and C20 re-planned from the slowest observed rates, scale20 run in its own phase on fewer workers (no shared load), and a structural change (stronger symmetry breaking) so that fewer conflicts are needed
brand: charcoal and sage; no purple, neon, emoji or gold
question: With B20 re-planned from 050's slowest rate (2000000), C20 re-planned from 050's slowest chunk rate (12000), scale20 run alone on 4 workers, and a new additive certify/16s (certify/16e plus BFS-canonical symmetry breaking), are 12 fresh 20-state worlds run wall-free (0 guard firings), deterministic over two passes, sound (non-vacuously) and decided at least once inside a 3600 s run? Separately, does certify/16n replicate on 12 fresh noisy 12-state worlds, and do 6 fresh controls all reach ID at B12 3000000?

hypotheses.H1: in an isolated scale20 phase on 4 workers at B20 = 2000000 and C20 = 12000, the 30 s chunk guard and 600 s case guard fire 0 times on every record (wall-free)
hypotheses.H2: two independent certify/16s passes give byte-identical canon16s records on 12/12 scale20 cases; controls and noise12 are byte-identical across passes
hypotheses.H3: scale20: WRONG = 0, every decided record audited true at bound 20, and at least 1 of 12 decided (non-vacuous); the decided count beyond 1 is reported, not predicted
hypotheses.H4: on the 6 control traces, certify/16s returns the same label and the same machine (canonical form) as the part-k certify/16e records (symmetry breaking removes only isomorphic copies)
hypotheses.H5: certify/16n (unchanged, FREEZE_050) issues no WRONG certificate on 12 fresh noisy 12-state worlds over two passes (replication of 050's GN12_sound)

design.api: no change to certify/16e (FREEZE_049) or certify/16n (FREEZE_050). One additive module brute/api/certify16s.py (certify/16s, Certifier16S): the certify/16e chunked-resume loop over a new encoding module that keeps the a16d variables and first-visit clauses and adds BFS-canonical symmetry breaking (parent and minimum-symbol variables, states numbered in BFS order of the hypothesis automaton; Ulyantsev, Zakirzyanov and Shalyto 2015 style). It is sound because every machine has exactly one BFS-canonical numbering, so the clauses remove only isomorphic copies; uniqueness up to isomorphism is unchanged (Inferred, checked by GCOMPAT16S and by the CNF reference at bound 20). Host-agnostic: no I/O, threads, subprocess or os in brute/; no frozen file edited
design.runtime_fix: (1) B20 and C20 re-planned from 050's slowest observed rates (cap_rule); (2) the main run has two phases: phase A runs only the scale20 jobs on 4 workers, phase B runs controls, compat and noise12 on 8 workers after phase A ends, so 20-state cases share the host only with each other (Inferred: 050's slow cases ran beside 7 other jobs; whether load is the cause is Open and is measured by GRATE51); (3) certify/16s needs fewer conflicts per decision (Inferred, Open; measured by GS20_rate51). The wall guards stay at 600 s per case and 30 s per call, host safety only; records exclude wall fields; any firing is a gate failure, never a label
design.cap_rule: fixed NOW, before any 051 data, from sealed 050 results only (Exact inputs, rule from plan 050 next_if_fail): B20 = 2000000 (4503 conflicts/s x 600 s x 0.75 = 2026350, rounded down to 2000000; worst case 444.2 s); C20 = 12000 (550 conflicts/s x 30 s x 0.75 = 12375, rounded down; worst case 21.8 s per chunk at the slowest chunk rate); B12 for controls = 3000000 (2x 050's B12, because 11750001 spent 1500135 without deciding; worst case 99.2 s at 30256/s); noise12 keeps certify/16n's frozen B12 = 1500000 and C = 50000 (replication, unchanged). Not calibrated, not tuned; the pre-freeze smoke never changes them

Phase B: controls 12 x (3000000 / 30256 + 10) = 12 x 109.2 = 1310; compat 6 x 109.2 = 655; noise12 24 x (1500000 / 30256 + 10) = 24 x 59.6 = 1430; total 3395 job-seconds on 8 workers, LPT about 425 s plus at most one 109 s tail, about 534 s. next_if_fail: GDET51 or GQB25 fails on guard firings in the isolated phase: wall time is not controllable by conflicts on this host even alone; next, scale20 gets its own version with 1 worker and a conflict-only stop, and no 20-state claim until 0 firings. GDET51 fails with 0 guard firings: certify/16s or the phase split is not deterministic; find the source, ship nothing new. GCOMPAT16S or GFID51 fails: symmetry breaking or replay is unfaithful; fix it, ship nothing new. GS20_sound51 or GN12_sound51 fails on WRONG: soundness first; do not scale further. GS20_sound51 fails on non-vacuity only (0/12 decided, WRONG 0): 20 states stay out of reach at 2000000 conflicts even with BFS symmetry breaking; next, a different encoding or search (for example an APTA or state-merging lower bound), not more budget. G_RT fails: publish it; the noise study gets its own version

claim_scope: conditional on the declared N: an ID or IDF means unique among machines with at most N states consistent with the (majority-corrected, for certify/16n) trace. Inferred reason: a larger machine can copy the true machine on every visited state and differ only where the trace never reaches, so a size bound is inherent. certify/16n claims are further conditional on the iid noise model with eps <= eps_bar and hold with probability >= 1 - delta
